title: Best Part's the Before

lyrics:
[Intro: one bright guitar chord pulsing, filtered synth rising]

[Verse 1: male lead, lightly tuned, no drums yet]
I've got a hunch about the evening
The mirror says we're looking right
Somebody's ironing in the hallway
Somebody's singing to the light

[Chorus: group vocals, kick drum enters]
The best part's the before
Shoes by the door
Somebody's playlist, somebody pour
We haven't even left yet
And I couldn't ask for more
The best part's the before

[Verse 2: female lead, full beat, claps]
The cab's been waiting twenty minutes
My sister's on her second dress
There's glitter on the bathroom ceiling
And I don't want to clean this mess

[Chorus: group vocals, full beat, synth stabs]
The best part's the before
Shoes by the door
Somebody's playlist, somebody pour
We haven't even left yet
And I couldn't ask for more
The best part's the before

[Chant: counting the hours, everyone shouting]
Five o'clock (what?) six o'clock (what?)
Seven, eight, nine and we're still not out the door
Ten o'clock (what?) who cares (what?)
Turn it up and do it all once more

[Bridge: beat drops out, toast, glasses clinking]
Fill it up (fill it up)
Raise it high (raise it high)
Salud, cheers, skol, slainte
To the ones who showed up tonight

[Build: snare roll, synth rising, one line repeated]
We haven't even left yet
We haven't even left yet
We haven't even left yet

[Final Chorus: biggest, everyone, synths wide open]
The best part's the before
Shoes by the door
Somebody's playlist, somebody pour
We haven't even left yet
And I couldn't ask for more
The best part's the before
The best part's the before

[Outro: guitar chord alone, door slam, car horn]
Okay. Now we can go.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 128 BPM, 4/4, G major. The same four chords from start to finish. Bright, rising, communal.

VOICE: A mixed group. A male lead with a smooth, lightly pitch-corrected tone opens. A female lead with a bright, brassy voice takes verse 2. Choruses and chants are sung and shouted by everyone, with crowd-style replies in brackets.

INSTRUMENTS: A clean electric guitar pulsing one bright chord at a time. A filtered synth that opens up through the song. A four-on-the-floor house kick, claps and off-beat hi-hats. A big, simple saw-wave synth bass. Wide synth stabs in the choruses. Clinking glasses, a door and a car horn as effects.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar chord and rising filter. 0:15 Verse 1, no drums. 0:30 Chorus 1, the kick enters. 0:52 Verse 2, full beat. 1:07 Chorus 2. 1:30 Chant, counting the hours. 1:45 Bridge, the beat drops for the toast. 2:07 Build, one line over a snare roll. 2:15 Final chorus, twice through. 3:00 Instrumental ride-out. 3:22 Outro, the guitar chord alone, a door, a horn and a spoken line at 3:40.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-2000s electro-pop: glossy, loud and wide, vocals tuned and layered, low end built for a hall PA.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The kick drum arriving under the first chorus at 0:30.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original promises a great night. This one notices, as people do with age, that the anticipation is the great part, and that the people in the hallway are the point.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Anticipation, more anticipation, gratitude, departure.
